_comment: Navigation sweep profile for Dr. Mario (1990) (Nintendo) - ADR-0239, PRD
Part A slice F14.17. Read by scripts/record_navigation_sweep.py.
RUNG 1, NOT RUNG 2. ADR-0239 s1 says to use the first rung that reaches the
place, and Dr. Mario's places are reached by rung 1: the game's own menu, by
input. navigation.kind is 'input', so no cheat rides with any session and
every session is an ADR-0184 s2 'clean' pass that all four surfaces may
read. Rung 2 would also be available - DataCrystal publishes the level -
but the ladder stops at the first rung that works, so nothing here pins a
byte.
THE SELECTOR, read off this ROM's own screens on 2026-09-26 (screenshots
under runs/f1417/drmario/probe/, unversioned) and the instruction booklet
(Nintendo of America, 1990; archive.org, item
'compilation-of-game-manuals-for-mini-consoles-english-only', file
'Nintendo - NES Classic Mini/Dr. Mario CLV-P-NAAXE_text.pdf'):
title screen   'Dr. MARIO' over '1 PLAYER GAME / 2 PLAYER GAME / (c) 1990
Nintendo'. The booklet: 'Here, you can select a 1 or 2
PLAYER game by using the SELECT Button. Then press the
START Button to move to the menu screen.' The ROM accepts a
Down press as well as SELECT (measured 2026-09-26: Down then
Start reaches the screen titled '2 PLAYER GAME'); no value
here needs it, because every place this sweep records is a
1 PLAYER game.
menu screen    titled '1 PLAYER GAME', with three rows: 'VIRUS LEVEL' over
a 1P scale from 00 to 20, 'SPEED' over 'LOW MED HI', and
'MUSIC TYPE' over 'FEVER CHILL OFF'. The cursor opens on
VIRUS LEVEL. The booklet: 'VIRUS LEVEL - The higher the
number, the more viruses you start with. Move the arrow mark
by using the Control Pad.'
the bottle     Start leaves the menu; the level the cursor left is the
level the game is played at, and 'VIRUS nn' on the clipboard
is 4 x (level + 1) viruses.
THE VALUES: all 21 virus levels the cursor reaches, 00 through 20 - not the
0/5/10/15/20 subset the slice's brief allowed. A level costs one press of
Right and the presses are free, so the subset would have bought nothing but a
smaller answer: the higher levels are where a board full of viruses would show
up if anywhere, and 20 is the only one of the five that is the end of the
scale. The whole ladder is 21 sessions, about 21 x 120 emulated seconds.
Every entry script is mint-level-NN.txt, generated by gen-entries.py beside
this file, and every one is the same six-step menu path with N presses of
Right in the middle. Two measurements fix its shape. The cursor CLAMPS at
both ends and never wraps - 20 presses from 00 reach 20 and further presses
hold it there, and three presses of Left at 00 leave it at 00 - so N presses
reach level N exactly, with no arithmetic. And a press is 2 frames of hold
plus 38 of release, because a held direction auto-repeats: measured, a
120-frame hold of Right walked the cursor 17 steps.
THE RAM CHECK, and what it does and does not prove. Every value checks $0096
- DataCrystal's 'Virus level' - which the menu writes as the plain number the
cursor left. It is a byte the place sets and no session pins, which is what
ADR-0239 s4 prefers, and it does not move again for the rest of the run
(measured: it reads the selected level at frame 1803 and at the end of a
120 s session at levels 00, 05, 10 and 20).
What it does NOT prove: $0096 is set by the menu, so a run that reached the
menu and never pressed Start reads the level too, and level 00's check is
also satisfied by a run that never left the title screen. The behavioural
test for those cases is ADR-0239 s4's 'new' count, which is the gate; the
check is a second reading and is decisive for the 20 levels above 00.
The other published byte, $0316 'Level number', reads identical to $0096 in
every probe of 2026-09-26 (both are written by the same menu code), so it
would say the same thing and is left out rather than checked twice.
$0324 - the clipboard's 'VIRUS nn', in the decimal-as-hex encoding
DataCrystal documents ('10 viruses remaining = hex 10 = decimal 16') - is
the byte that DOES separate the menu from the bottle: it is 00 on the menu
and 4 x (level + 1) once the game starts, so it is decisive at level 00 too.
It is deliberately not the check. It is a live counter, not a constant: the
game decrements it as viruses die, and at frame 1803 a level 01 session read
07 and a level 15 session read 63 where the level sets 08 and 64 - one
virus each, cleared by the blind body's own stack. Its value at 120 s was
confirmed for levels 00, 05, 10 and 20 (04, 24, 44, 84 - exactly 4 x
(level + 1) in both the decimal and the BCD reading) and is reported for
each session beside the check rather than asserted.
WHAT IS NOT A VALUE, and why each is a modifier rather than a place. Each
of these was also recorded as a full 120 s session at level 00 so the
claim is a measurement (runs/f1417/drmario/not-swept.log):
SPEED (LOW / MED / HI)  The booklet: 'This controls the speed at which the
vitamin capsules drop.' It changes how fast the same
bottle is played. LOW and HI do move the archive -
339 and 342 keys level 00 does not hold - but 332
of LOW's 339 just re-pair a tile level 00 already
draws with one of three palettes level 00 does not,
and both rows name only 2 new tile-data strings
each. The control is SPEED MED, which is the place
level 00 is already at: it is byte-identical to the
baseline and still reads 8 new keys, so that is the
floor of re-recording, not a contribution. Every
value here is recorded at the default, MED.
MUSIC TYPE (FEVER /     The booklet: 'Choose between two musical selections
CHILL / OFF)            ... You can also turn the music OFF.' It selects a
track. Measured at 120 s: 10 and 7 new keys, 2 and 0
new tile-data strings. Nothing it can do reaches a
texture.
2 PLAYER GAME           The title screen's second option, one press of
SELECT away, and NOT a value of this profile: the
swept axis is the VIRUS LEVEL row of a 1 PLAYER
GAME. It is the biggest measured gap here. At 120 s
and level 00 it writes 1137 keys, 171 of them new
against level 00 on zero new palettes, naming 116
CHR indices level 00 never draws - 115 of them
outside the vocabulary of the whole 21-session
sweep, against 30 for all twenty levels above 00
together. A later slice that wants it adds one value
whose entry presses SELECT and checks $0727 = 02.
VS. COM                 The title screen's third option, a third mode, also
not swept and not measured.
NO LIVES PIN, so ADR-0239 s3's inert control does not apply. Dr. Mario has no
lives and no continues: a session is one bottle, and it ends when the viruses
are gone or the bottle fills. defaults.cheats is therefore absent and no
process in this sweep is launched with a cheat at all.
CAVEAT THAT APPLIES TO EVERY SESSION, and it is the same one the other
profiles carry. The bottle is entered, not played to an end, and ADR-0239 s5's
before side is the level-00 session of this same sweep (see the RESULT for
why that is the game's first place and not a separate recording). The
level-00 row therefore reads new = 0 BY CONSTRUCTION - it is the baseline
scored against itself - and not because a warp failed; Ninja Gaiden's profile
avoids the same row by leaving its stage-1 index out of values[], which this
profile does not do because the brief asks for the levels the menu reaches and
00 is one of them.
_provenanceComment: romSha1 is the No-Intro SHA1 of the user's library dump, computed on this
checkout 2026-09-26; the whole-file SHA1 of the same dump is
between the two. The ROM is never copied into the repository. The header
declares 2 PRG banks of 16 KB and 4 CHR banks of 8 KB, so 32768 bytes of
CHR and a ROM CHR denominator of 2048 16-byte patterns.

navigation.source: The game's own screens and the instruction booklet: 'After you power up the game, you'll see the title screen. Here, you can select a 1 or 2 PLAYER game by using the SELECT Button. Then press the START Button to move to the menu screen'; 'VIRUS LEVEL - The higher the number, the more viruses you start with. Move the arrow mark by using the Control Pad'; 'After making your selections, press the START Button to begin playing.' Dr. Mario instruction booklet (Nintendo of America, 1990), 'STARTING THE GAME'. Corroborated by this ROM's own screens, read 2026-09-26: the title's '1 PLAYER GAME / 2 PLAYER GAME', the menu's 'VIRUS LEVEL / SPEED / MUSIC TYPE' rows, and the clipboard's 'LEVEL nn / SPEED MED / VIRUS nn' in the bottle. ADR-0239 s1 rung 1: input, no cheat.

_defaultsComment: The entry default is the level-00 mint, which is the same menu path with no
press of Right: the game's own first place. No value uses it - every value
names its own mint-level-NN.txt, because the level IS the place - but it is
kept so the file stays a valid profile for a value added later, and because
level 00 is what the level-00 value's own entry is.
seconds is ADR-0239 s6's budget, 120 emulated seconds per session, and the
body is repeated by record_navigation_sweep.py until that budget is covered.
The body is scripts/stages/drmario/bottle-run.txt: the game's own controls
driven blind - A and B tapped to turn the pill through its four orientations,
Left and Right held to walk it to a wall, Down tapped to drop it fast. It
cannot aim a match, so the bottle fills and the game ends on GAME OVER inside
the 120 s at every level measured (00, 05, 10 and 20). That is ADR-0184 s4
doing its job: a clean pass is allowed to die, and the loss screen is real
